deer.text: It stares at you, chewing. It has a very Wicklow look, one that says it has seen worse weather and better hikers.

ranger.text: Wicklow Mountains National Park is the largest in Ireland, with peat bogs, heather, lakes and loads of sheep. We call this 'the Garden of Ireland'.
The sika deer are from Japan, originally. A few escaped from the Powerscourt estate in the 1860s, and they've been enjoying themselves ever since.

monk_guide.text: St Kevin founded the monastery in the 6th century. It became one of the great schools of early Ireland. Monks came from all over Europe.
The Vikings raided it many times. The monks said 'ah, here we go again' and rebuilt it. That's resilience.

lake_watcher.text: Red grouse, peregrines, ravens. And, once a year, a very confused kayaker.
Ravens are the clever ones. I once watched one open my rucksack zip. It took my sandwich and left the banana. Serves me right.

sheep_farmer.text: The sheep are Blackface. They're hardy, they're woolly, and they've decided the road is theirs.
I let them through at the cattle grid. They look at me like I'm the one who's late.
